supporting_evidence.summary: significant deviations in scope [all services]: productcatalogservice_latency-90 z=944.51 (4722.6%); productcatalogservice_latency-50 z=520.78 (2603.9%); recommendationservice_latency-90 z=455.66 (2278.3%); recommendationservice_latency-50 z=424.71 (2123.5%)
traces for productcatalogservice: SIGNIFICANT change; own spans self-time p50 0.01->0.02ms (1.25x), errors 0.0->0.0; inbound calls self-time p50 2.42->202.98ms (83.7x), errors 0.0->0.0

alternatives_rejected.why: Its latency deviation (z=455.66) is smaller than productcatalogservice's (z=944.51) in E1. That fits it being a caller slowed by productcatalogservice, whose inbound latency rose 83.7x (E2).

Own-span self-time barely moved (0.01->0.02ms, E2) while caller-observed latency rose about 200ms. No CPU metric appears among the top deviations in E1, only latency metrics. This pattern points to delay on the network path, not compute saturation.

proposed_fix.description: Inspect and remove the injected network delay on productcatalogservice, e.g. tc/netem qdisc rules or chaos experiments on its pod or interface. Then confirm that the callers' inbound latency returns to its ~2.4ms baseline.
